| DL-91 | 2026-09-06                          | **WS9 A4/A5 ROOT CAUSE — THE SIDE PANEL'S READERS WERE DRIVEN BY RENDERS, NOT BY EVIDENCE. FIXED, and the intermittency is gone.** **(1) THE SYMPTOM.** On real Windows Chromium (Playwright 1.62.0, Node 24.15.0) E2E-A4 was reproducibly intermittent inside its 20,000 ms budget (4 beats of `heartbeatMs`), and A5 failed purely downstream because its precondition never saw a standing claim. Measured latencies from `bringToFront` to the banner across runs: 283 ms, 357 ms, 558 ms, 568 ms, 843 ms, 24,872 ms, and twice NEVER within 40,000 ms. Bimodal, not slow. **(2) WHAT WAS ELIMINATED, BY MEASUREMENT AND NOT BY ARGUMENT.** Heartbeat failure (the observation stayed ~4 s fresh and `lastHeartbeatAt` advanced), missing or invalid durable evidence (every read HIT), the wrong durable key, the wrong tab (both panels resolved the fixture tab and `tabs.onActivated` fired correctly), hidden-tab timer throttling (throttling delays a timer, it does not delete one), an A4 assertion mismatch, an inadequate budget (doubling the window to 40 s changed nothing), and sender validation. Two of these were MY OWN earlier hypotheses and the owner's measurements disproved both; they are recorded here as rejected rather than quietly dropped. **(3) THE PROOF.** A read-only probe wrapped four `chrome` APIs in the panel page and counted. Four Windows runs returned 75 / 146 / 222, 88 / 174 / 261, 116 / 230 / 347 and 5,205 / 10,408 / 15,612 for runtime queries, observation reads and workflow reads — a ratio converging to exactly 1 : 2 : 3. That is the per-render cost of four readers re-arming TOGETHER: `useRecording` (1 query + 1 observation), `useRecordingFeedback` (1 observation + 1 workflow), `useExport` (1 workflow) and `useRecordingWorkspace` (1 workflow). The largest run therefore rendered 5,205 times in 24.9 seconds — 209 renders per second — against a documented beat of one read per 5,000 ms. **(4) THE MECHANISM.** `SidePanel.tsx` built a FRESH OBJECT LITERAL for each of the four hooks on every render. Each was an effect dependency, so every render tore down and re-armed all four effects, and each teardown sets `alive = false`, which DISCARDS the in-flight read. Three of the four hooks then set a freshly built object as state, so React could never bail out and the loop could never quiesce. `useRecording` is the only producer of the lifecycle view and the SLOWEST — it awaits a runtime round-trip — so its result was repeatedly preempted before it could commit. The view landed only when a round-trip happened to win a race against the loop: a geometric wait, which is precisely the observed distribution. **(5) THE CORRECTION, IN TWO PARTS BECAUSE ONE WOULD HAVE REGRESSED.** PART A: `SidePanel.tsx` now memoises ONE shared binding (`useMemo` on `panel.pick.tabId`; `storageGateway` is a module constant) and passes the same object to all four readers. PART B: `useExport` and `useRecordingWorkspace` had NO timer — their apparent freshness was a side effect of the storm, so Part A alone would have frozen the code workspace at its first read. They now read once and then follow WS4's EXISTING `gateway.watch` seam, the one `pick-source.ts` already uses for LAST_PICK and PICKER_ACTIVE; the listener receives the validated workflow directly, so a change costs no second read, and language stays out of the subscription because rendering the same recording in another language is a derivation, not a re-read. HARDENING: `useRecording`, `useRecordingFeedback`, `useExport` and `useRecordingWorkspace` now depend on the BINDING (tab id, gateway, injected clock) rather than on the object that carries it, so a future caller passing a literal cannot bring the storm back. **(6) MEASURED EFFECT, same probe, same machine class.** Before: 113 runtime sends and 559 storage reads inside 577 ms, 98 of those queries against the fixture tab. After: 2 sends and 10 reads TOTAL — exactly one round per binding, one before the activation and one after. Banner at 260 ms. **(7) WHAT DID NOT MOVE.** LIVE > DURABLE > UNKNOWN, the DL-89 unconfirmed-banner rule, UNTRUSTED_SENDER, fail-closed recording, the verified-locator requirement, the heartbeat constants, `tabs.ts`, the message contracts, the durable schema and `RECORDING_ENABLED = false` are all untouched. That is bounded entirely by constants that already exist: `hardStop` (100) caps the number of workflow writes, `fillDebounceMs` already coalesces rapid typing into one action AT THE MODEL BOUNDARY so keystrokes never become writes, `heartbeatMs` (5 s) sets the observation cadence, and `maxWorkflowBytes` (500 KB) already bounds the size. **No new byte limit was needed and none was invented.** **SERIALISATION IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED.** A populated workflow round-trips through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` byte-for-byte, and chain, verdict, counts, stepCounts and rationale codes are compared field by field.
